title: Algorithmic tipping point analysis for optimizing the patient journey in multimorbidity
summary:
Background: Introduction of the provision set out in Section 25b of the German Social Code Book V (SGB V) through the Health Data Use Act (GDNG), and the resulting possibility for statutory health and long-term care insurers to identify individual health risks on a data-based basis.
Research Question: Is it possible to identify the risks of tipping points in care that could lead to significantly increased and preventable burdens, as well as health limitations, among patients with multimorbidity? How can the identified health risk be communicated to patients in a way that is understandable and transparent? How can acceptance of this approach also be fostered among treating primary care physicians?
Methodology: Prospective intervention study using a mixed-methods design with process evaluation; qualitative and quantitative surveys of participating insured individuals and primary care physicians.
conditions: This study focuses on multimorbid patients who have at least three chronic conditions within a one-year period. A list of chronic conditions to be considered was adopted from Ho et al. (2022).

interventions.name: A notice to insured individuals pursuant to Section 25b of SGB V, referring to a potentially increased health risk. The notice is expected to be sent out once, in July 2027.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of insured individuals with multimorbidity based on the years 2021–2025 (algorithm development).
Documented multimorbidity; algorithmic indication of an increased risk of crossing a health tipping point.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals under the age of 18, individuals without documented multimorbidity.
